sentences.text: BECHU KURIAN THOMAS, J.
ORDER Petitioner is the Branch Manager of M/s. Sundaram Finance Limited which is stated to be a non-banking financial company registered with the Reserve Bank of India.

According to the prosecution, the accused was found in possession of 287 blank cheques and 25 filled up cheques and the same were collected in an attempt to cheat the depositors and to demand exorbitant interest and thereby committed the offences under Section 13 of the Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958 apart from Section 511 of 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. I have heard Sri.S.Sreekumar, the learned Senior counsel duly instructed by Sri.P.Martin Jose as well as Sri.Ranjith T.R., the learned Public Prosecutor.
3.

In the decision in Nedumpilli Finance Company Ltd. v. State of Kerala [(2022) 7 SCC 394], the Supreme Court has observed that the non-banking financial companies are registered under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 and regulated by the Reserve Bank of India.

entities.text: Nedumpilli Finance Company Ltd. v. State of Kerala [(2022) 7 SCC 394]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958 cannot have any application.

It is further observed in the said decision that the "the fact that RBI generally leaves it to the market forces to determine the rate of interest, without CRL.MC NO. 3050 OF 2015 any direct intervention, is not something that could be taken advantage of by the State of Kerala to step in and prescribe the maximum rate of interest chargeable by NBFCs on the loans advanced by them".

4. In view of the above decision and the observations extracted therein, it is evident that the petitioner cannot be stated to have attempted to charge exorbitant interest or commit any offence under the Kerala Money Lenders Act,1958 especially since there is no reference at all to the rate of interest charged or permitted by the RBI during the relevant period.

5. Further, the possession of blank cheques by itself cannot be indicative of any attempt to cheat as the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 confer power upon the holder of a blank cheque to fill up the same.
As long as holder of the cheque acts in accordance with the authorisation given to him, no offence can be said to be committed merely by possessing blank cheques.
Therefore, the prosecution against the petitioner is an abuse of the process of the court.
6. In view of the above, the proceedings against the petitioners in Crime No.1640 of 2014 of Karunagappally Police Station shall stand quashed.
The Crl.M.C.is allowed.

BECHU KURIAN THOMAS, J.
=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=
 Crl.M.C.No.3050 of 2015  =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=
 Dated this the 17th day of January, 2024
ORDER Petitioner is the Branch Manager of M/s. Sundaram Finance Limited which is stated to be a non-banking financial company registered with the Reserve Bank of India.
According to the prosecution, the accused was found in possession of 287 blank cheques and 25 filled up cheques and the same were collected in an attempt to cheat the depositors and to demand exorbitant interest and thereby committed the offences under Section 13 of the Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958 apart from Section 511 of 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2. I have heard Sri.S.Sreekumar, the learned Senior counsel duly instructed by Sri.P.Martin Jose as well as Sri.Ranjith T.R., the learned Public Prosecutor.
3.
In the decision in Nedumpilli Finance Company Ltd. v. State of Kerala [(2022) 7 SCC 394], the Supreme Court has observed that the non-banking financial companies are registered under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 and regulated by the Reserve Bank of India.
The Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958 cannot have any application.
It is further observed in the said decision that the "the fact that RBI generally leaves it to the market forces to determine the rate of interest, without CRL.MC NO. 3050 OF 2015 any direct intervention, is not something that could be taken advantage of by the State of Kerala to step in and prescribe the maximum rate of interest chargeable by NBFCs on the loans advanced by them".
5. Further, the possession of blank cheques by itself cannot be indicative of any attempt to cheat as the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 confer power upon the holder of a blank cheque to fill up the same.
As long as holder of the cheque acts in accordance with the authorisation given to him, no offence can be said to be committed merely by possessing blank cheques.
Therefore, the prosecution against the petitioner is an abuse of the process of the court.
